expects.query:
Deploy the VSS base profile on `{{platform}}` with VIOS and a video-understanding VLM ready for the following vss-ask-video queries. Use the configured remote model endpoints and run autonomously.

**Unified memory is a prerequisite for this spec.** The stock `base` profile ships no memory backend, so extend it with the `elasticsearch` and `elasticsearch-init-container` service keys, then wire the CLI to it. Re-running `vss configure` after the deploy is required, not optional: the CLI records the backends it discovers at the base URL, so a deployment that gained Elasticsearch after the last `configure` still reports "records no Elasticsearch" and every memory call fails.

```bash
VSS_REPO_ROOT="${VSS_REPO_ROOT:-$HOME/video-search-and-summarization}"
VSS=(uv run --project "${VSS_REPO_ROOT}/libs/vss" vss)

# The deployment's ingress, and whichever configured LLM endpoint answers.
# Wait for warmup on the same budget the readiness check below allows -
# probing once can leave JUDGE empty and make the next command fail.
BASE_URL="http://${HOST_IP:-localhost}:7777"
JUDGE=""
end=$((SECONDS+570))
while [ -z "${JUDGE}" ] && [ ${SECONDS} -lt ${end} ]; do
  for u in http://localhost:30081/v1 http://localhost:30082/v1 http://localhost:8018/v1; do
    curl -sf --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 5 "${u}/models" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
      && { JUDGE="${u}"; break; }
  done
  [ -z "${JUDGE}" ] && sleep 5
done
[ -n "${JUDGE}" ] || { echo 'no LLM endpoint became ready' >&2; exit 1; }

"${VSS[@]}" configure --base-url "${BASE_URL}"
"${VSS[@]}" configure memory --enable --backend elasticsearch --index vss-memory
"${VSS[@]}" configure memory introspection --enable --judge-endpoint "${JUDGE}"
```

`--judge-endpoint` is required the first time introspection is configured; the loop above waits up to the same 9.5 minutes the readiness check allows and takes whichever of this deployment's OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints comes up first, so a cold model does not leave it empty. Confirm with `vss memory query --query anything` returning exit 0 - a successful `configure memory show` only proves the file was written, not that a backend is reachable.
checks: `curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns exit 0 (VIOS is responsive).

`timeout 570s sh -c 'while :; do for url in http://localhost:30081/v1/models http://localhost:30082/v1/models http://localhost:8018/v1/models; do curl -sf --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 5 "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; done; sleep 5; done'` returns exit 0 (at least one configured video-understanding VLM becomes ready; polls for up to 9.5 minutes to absorb model warmup).

`sh -c 'VSS_REPO_ROOT="${VSS_REPO_ROOT:-$HOME/video-search-and-summarization}"; uv run --project "${VSS_REPO_ROOT}/libs/vss" vss memory query --query readiness-probe'` returns exit 0. This is a real round-trip against the configured backend, so it fails when Elasticsearch is absent or the CLI has not re-discovered it - unlike `configure memory show`, which returns 0 whenever the config file was written and would pass while every later memory step still fails with "cannot reach unified memory".
